- **Last week, after many years of missing out, I finally made it to Anticipation Conference . The beauty of such a gathering is that it is non-trivial to write a post about the experience. There are conferences that can be readily boiled down into easily digestible bits for consumption on social platforms, but this is not one of them. At once, it is theoretical, experimental, applied, philosophical, embodied, hopeful... the list goes on. And for someone who works with #futures and #foresight , it is always a breath of fresh air to walk into spaces where you feel no expectation of certainty. In fact, sitting with #uncertainty is the whole point. There are far too many people to call out, both new friends and old, that made those few days invaluable. I will be reflecting on the new ideas and inspirations for months, at least. All to say, I highly recommend the conference if you want to challenge yourself with the latest thinking at the edge of anticipation. A big thank you to Manuela Celi , Politecnico di Milano , and the entire organizing team for hosting a fantastic event!**

- **"Full futures literacy is a cognitive and organizational property, and it develops through sustained practice." Like Kyle Brown , I've been hearing the term "futures literacy" used a lot more and, like "foresight," it is still not generally well understood. If you are looking for a brief, masterful articulation of what Futures Literacy is and is not, this is it. In fact, if you work with Futures and Foresight, I would make this required reading for all of your stakeholders. As Kyle says, Futures Literacy cannot emerge as an organizational property if treated as an episodic exercise. It won't come from the next workshop and it definitely won't come from reading more reports. The same can be said of Foresight. "It is slow to build and hard to measure," but playing the cultural long game is the only path to real, lasting transformation. I cannot recommend this blog post enough. Read it. #futures #futuresliteracy #foresight #leadership #culture #transformation**

- **Recently I had the pleasure of sharing the stage with Mirkka Schaller, PhD and Agathe Acchiardo at NEXT Pharma Summit for a dialogue about Why #Pharma Needs #Foresight , Not Forecasts. To be clear, forecasting has its place but is insufficient to navigate the rapids ahead for the industry. Leaders need to develop an advanced ability to make decisions before uncertainties are, or at least appear to be, resolved. But why now? After all, as Stefani Klaskow and Lois Gregory put it in their presentation on the New Language of Health: "Things are changing. Said everyone ever." Add to that Florent Edouard 's concise 20-year history of "transformation theater," littered with expensive technology initiative failures, and one is left to wonder whether the present moment offers anything different. For all the promises of tech, what could make today uniquely transformative is a renewed focus on the human element of change. This was evident from Serena Planera and Arantxa Mugica Goicoechea 's "human realities" of digital transformation, to Jennifer Cleall 's warning that technology won't fix a broken operating model, to Iroda Jurabekova 's observation that systems fluency is needed to build for adaptability and optionality. Today's opportunity with technology, therefore, does not lie in making the traditional model more efficient. Rather, if we humans have the courage to more openly listen to the change around us, re-imagine what value we could create and how, and organize around building it, then even if the tech doesn't live up to the hype we just may see a transformed pharma industry emerge. Big thanks to Dario , Petra , and team for bringing everyone together for such an insightful experience! #pharma #transformation #TeamUCB**

- **On Monday, the eighth edition of the AXA Foresight Report was launched to an audience overflowing from a small dome at ChangeNOW . The immersion brought one of their New Future Archetypes to life, sparking an all too brief dialogue about the importance of situating our imaginaries in local ecologies, including reflections about intergeneration fairness and what it could mean to be a responsible ancestor. Even in a crowded, time-constrained setting, it was an encouraging conversation, and a welcome challenge to make these spaces a more frequent phenomenon both inside organizations and in public. Thanks to Olivier Desbiey for the invitation and congratulations to AXA, N O R M A L S , and the extended team behind the report. As a teaser for those who have yet to read it, here's an excerpt from the introduction that struck a chord: "But for archetypes to function as tools for our imagination, there is a critical requirement: rather than force-fitting ideas into old boxes to confirm existing categories, we must use what we observe to create new distinctions. We need to think of archetypes not as eternal, basic shapes but as evolving cores of what we can imagine. The question then shifts away from ‘which box can we sort this future into?’ to ‘which new boxes can we imagine to hold new futures?’" We definitely need new boxes. #AXAForesight2026**

- **“What's it like working at an agency?” About a year ago my career shifted quite significantly. 🛫 I moved out of the big brand world I had been inside for nearly two decades, into a start-up-ish strategic consultancy. Friends and ex-colleagues inside the big corporate brand world ask me often what that feels like. I didn't do the traditional stint in agency-land when I started my career, I went straight from uni to the biggest paper goods company in the world which kick started my marketing journey. Things on this side are very different. It’s making me wonder if large corporates can operate like a start up agency. Because there are a lot of things I wish I had had in my big brands days. 🍟 ✅ Getting things done really quickly. (Literally I just ask the CEO and he says 'yes if it makes sense, let's try it'.) ✅ An appetite for innovation. And therefore constant energy. (Often, before the business case.) ✅ Provoking … not just providing the answer. In this way, being judged for your intellect not your intel. It's really nice to see what it's like on the other side. And it helps to do it at a company that has a ton of fun and moves FAST.**

- **From 1 to 3 July 2026, the Department of Design at Politecnico di Milano hosted the sixth edition of Anticipation Conference , one of the leading international events dedicated to anticipation studies. Bringing together more than 300 participants from 35 countries, the conference, chaired by Manuela Celi, explored how design can engage with uncertainty not as a problem to eliminate, but as a condition for imagining and shaping alternative futures. Under the theme 'Staying with the Unknown: Paradox, Uncertainty, and the Praxis of Hope', researchers, designers, philosophers, public institutions and professionals discussed the evolving role of design across futures literacy, governance, ecological transitions, care, world-making and more-than-human perspectives. Hosting Anticipation 2026 reaffirms the Department of Design's commitment to positioning design as a transdisciplinary practice capable of framing emerging challenges, expanding collective imaginaries, and contributing to more just and sustainable futures. A special thank you to our keynote speakers and the UNESCO Chairs for joining the conversation and enriching the discussion with their valuable, inspiring insights and expertise. So many insights to chew on from the inspiring keynotes of Betti Marenko Ivana Milojević and Fabio Scarano and the countless sessions and workshops. So many new faces and young enthusiasts that are ready to embark on this journey. We need more and different voices, more research, more experiments and more stories!
